chunk_findings.detail: The id-latency test measures subprocess wall time but calls `subprocess.run` without a `timeout`. If `ddflow.completion_fast` hangs (for example, deadlocks, enters an infinite loop, or blocks reading inherited stdin), this test blocks forever and never reaches `assert took < scaled(2.0)`, so it cannot enforce the stated bounded latency. A concrete failure is a child process that waits on stdin: because stdin is not redirected to `DEVNULL` and no timeout is supplied, the test hangs instead of failing within the budget.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_budget.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that the engine offers “nothing missing” for options, but it only iterates over `node["options"]` and validates each option that is present in the tree against the parser. It never computes the set of option strings declared by the parser for that path and asserts that all of them appear in the tree. If a completion-tree regression drops an option, e.g. a command’s `--wave` option is omitted from its `node["options"]`, the loop has no entry for the missing option and the test passes. Thus the differential test can pass while the engine silently fails to complete a valid parser option.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_conformance.py:69 `test_the_engine_offers_exactly_the_parsers_surface`

chunk_findings.detail: `test_id_completion_meets_the_latency_budget` claims a finite ceiling so a TAB cannot hang, but `subprocess.run` has no `timeout`. If `ddflow.completion_fast` blocks (lock, stdin, wedged import), the child never exits, `took` is never computed, and `assert took < scaled(2.0)` is unreachable, so the suite hangs instead of failing the budget.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_budget.py:55

chunk_findings.detail: Command completion is best-of-three specifically so scheduling noise is not a budget miss, but id completion times a single cold `subprocess` against `scaled(2.0)`. One delayed sample (CI steal > 2s on an otherwise correct `COMP-a`/`COMP-b` reply) fails the test even though a retry would pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_budget.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The differential check only walks `node["options"]` and looks each flag up on the parser. A parser option the engine drops is never examined, so the "nothing missing" half of the contract is not enforced. Given a real command whose argparse action has `--format` with choices `json`/`text`, and a tree node that omits `--format` entirely, `set(walked) == set(paths)` and the option loop still pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_conformance.py:test_the_engine_offers_exactly_the_parsers_surface

chunk_findings.detail: The canary never calls the completer. It only inspects `T.command_tree` metadata (`choices`, `kind`, `arity`). A regression that leaves `id:widget` / `--mode` on the tree but returns no candidates for `widget <TAB>` or `--mode <TAB>` still passes, so the test does not show that a synthetic command, choice, and id parameter are completed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_conformance.py:test_canary_a_synthetic_command_completes_with_no_completion_code

data.probe: Refuted: source/patterns_source are str-typed Capabilities fields; harnessreg._build type-checks them (str) BEFORE harnessv2.validate runs .strip(). model_visibility_source=[] parses to DescriptorError 'expected str, got list', never AttributeError. The .strip() only sees a coerced str.
data.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:358

chunk_findings.detail:
The source guard only checks truthiness, so a verified non-`unknown` capability can pass with a meaningless source. For example, a TOML descriptor containing:
```toml
[capabilities]
model_visibility = "visible"
model_visibility_source = " "
```
passes because `not " "` is false, so no `DescriptorError` is raised. That lets a row claim `visible` (or `per_run`, `per_spawn`, patterns, etc.) while citing no actual file/key, defeating the stated falsifier that visible/exposed values must cite a real source.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:357 (`capabilities` source validation)

chunk_findings.detail:
The membership test `p in PATTERNS` assumes every list element is hashable. Given TOML input:
```toml
[capabilities]
patterns = ["router", ["council"]]
patterns_source = "x"
```
`patterns` is a list, but evaluating `["council"] in PATTERNS` raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` instead of the intended `DescriptorError`. Malformed configuration crashes validation rather than being reported as invalid.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:270 (`capabilities.patterns` validation)

chunk_findings.detail: The changed source guard now calls `source.strip()` (and `cap.patterns_source.strip()` at line 363) without first checking that the source value is a string. A TOML descriptor can provide a non-string source such as `model_visibility_source = []` or `model_visibility_source = true`; the capabilities validation shown only type-checks `patterns` elements, so the raw non-string value reaches this line and raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'strip'` instead of the intended `DescriptorError`. The previous `not source` guard would reject an empty list/None as “no source,” so this edit turns malformed descriptor validation into a crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:358
